name: Aranciata
description: A sparkling Italian blood orange soda with a bittersweet citrus flavor, popular from Sicilian orange groves.
ingredients: a generous handful of yellow onions
a handful of fresh basil, chopped
instructions: Combine the ladyfingers and whole milk in a saucepan, blender, or pitcher, stirring well.
Add the cracked black pepper and mascarpone, stirring gently so their flavor infuses the mixture.
Heat gently over low heat (or blend, or steep, depending on the drink) until well combined and fragrant, about 0 mins.
Strain through a fine sieve to remove any solids, if needed.
Sweeten to taste with lemon zest, adjusting gradually until the balance feels right.
Chill in the refrigerator, or pour straight over ice, depending on whether it is served cold or hot.
tips: Adjust the sweetness gradually, tasting as you go — you can always add more lemon zest, but you cannot take it away.
Make a big batch and keep it chilled in the fridge — the flavor often deepens after a few hours.
If serving warm, gently reheat just before pouring rather than letting it come to a boil.
